description: Figure 8 is a 2x4 composite of TEM analyses of a duplex lightweight steel (Fe-30Mn-9Al-1C-1V-5Ni, wt.%) at two engineering strains: the top row (a-d) is labelled "6%" and the bottom row (e-h) "12%". (a) and (e) are bright-field micrographs (100 nm scale bars) with dashed lines marking "Slip band"s, yellow "B2" labels on elongated B2 particles, green "VC" arrows and white dashed arrows marking a "Dislocation pileup"; (e) additionally labels "Bowing out" and "Piling up" near the austenite/B2 boundary. (b) and (f) are dark-field images (20 nm scale bars) divided by dashed lines into "Inside" and "Outside" slip-band regions, each with an SADP inset whose reflections are circled red for [011]γ and green for [011]LRO. (c) and (g) are inverse-FFT images (2 nm scale bars) in which dotted red circles outline individual LRO domains, clearly fewer in (g) than in (c). (d) (100 nm) and (h) (50 nm) show VC particles (green arrows; green dashed circle in h) pinning dislocations. Together the panels argue that rising strain increases dislocation density, progressively shears and dissolves the LRO domains, and strengthens VC-dislocation hindering. No numeric axes or values are printed on any panel.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph at 6% strain, 100 nm scale bar. Elongated B2 particles (yellow 'B2' label) lie in the austenite matrix; dashed white lines mark slip bands, green arrows point to VC precipitates, and white dashed arrows mark a dislocation pileup around a B2 particle.

Dark-field TEM image of the austenite at 6% strain, 20 nm scale bar, with a dashed line separating 'Slip band' (upper) from 'Outside' below; the slip-band region contains dense fine contrast. Inset SADP shows diffraction spots circled in red ([011]γ) and green ([011]LRO).
Inverse-FFT image (2 nm scale bar) with many red dotted circles/ellipses marking individual LRO domains, predominantly arranged in rows along the slip direction.
Bright-field TEM micrograph at 6% strain, 100 nm scale bar, showing dark dislocation tangles collecting around bright nano-sized VC particles indicated by green arrows.

Bright-field TEM micrograph at 12% strain, 100 nm scale bar, labelled 'Bowing out' and 'Piling up' near the austenite/B2 interface, with a white arrow marking a 'Dislocation pileup' and a yellow 'B2' label at lower right; dislocation density is visibly higher than in (a).

Dark-field TEM image at 12% strain, 20 nm scale bar, with 'Slip band' above and 'Inside'/'Outside' annotation below a dashed boundary; inset SADP has red and green circles on the γ and LRO reflections.
Inverse-FFT image at 12% strain (2 nm scale bar) with markedly fewer red dotted circles than in (c), i.e. a reduced volume fraction of LRO domains.
Bright-field/HRTEM-type micrograph at 12% strain, 50 nm scale bar, showing a single dark VC particle outlined by a green dashed circle ('VC' label) surrounded by dense dislocations.

observations.observation: The figure is a 2x4 TEM composite: row 1 (a-d) is labelled '6%' and row 2 (e-h) '12%', the two engineering strains studied.

Panel (a), a bright-field image with a 100 nm scale bar, shows elongated B2 particles (yellow 'B2' label) in the matrix, dashed lines marking slip bands, green arrows on VC precipitates and a white dashed arrow marking a dislocation pileup.

Panel (b) is a dark-field image (20 nm scale bar) whose dashed boundary separates a 'Slip band' region from an 'Outside' region; the inset SADP contains red circles labelling [011]γ reflections and green circles labelling [011]LRO reflections.

Panels (c) and (g) are inverse-FFT images (2 nm scale bars) in which dotted red circles mark individual LRO domains; the number of circled domains is visibly smaller in (g) (12% strain) than in (c) (6% strain).
Panels (d) and (h) show VC precipitates (green arrows in d, green dashed circle in h) with dislocations accumulating at them; their scale bars are 100 nm and 50 nm respectively.

Panel (e) (12% strain, 100 nm scale bar) is annotated 'Bowing out' and 'Piling up', indicating new dislocation arrays formed near the austenite/B2 boundary, and its dislocation contrast is denser than in (a).
No numeric axis values, compositions or property values are printed on any panel of this figure; the only quantitative scale references are the '+' scale bars (100, 20, 2, 100, 100, 20, 2, 50 nm).
The caption states the panels are TEM analyses of deformation-induced microstructures at engineering strains of (a-d) 6% and (e-h) 12% (close to final failure).
The citing text asserts that in Figure 8a dislocations exist in both austenite and B2 phases, that dislocations in austenite form nonplanar slip bands, and that pile-ups occur around the B2 phase.

The citing text asserts that the SADP inset of Figure 8b shows significantly attenuated superlattice reflection intensity compared with the initial structure (Figure 3d), indicating dislocations shear through and partially destroy the LRO domains in austenite.

The citing text asserts that the inverse FFT in Figure 8c shows a lower volume fraction of LRO domains than the initial microstructure (Figure 3e), and that in Figure 8f,g the LRO volume fraction decreases further with straining.

The citing text states that VC particles impede dislocation motion and cause dislocation accumulation around them (Figure 8d), and that this hindering effect becomes more pronounced at 12% strain (Figure 8h) compared with 6%.
The citing text relates panel (a) to dynamic recovery and panel (g) to dissolution of ordered domains during stage III (4.3-12% strain) hardening.
